source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: Chapter 4 exercise hal (PDF 92-94): MCQs hisaab ke saath, short aur descriptive jawab, numericals qadam ba qadam, Kitab ki ghalti aur Wazahat boxes.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 4 (Stoichiometry) ki exercise hai, kitab ki tarteeb mein, hal ke saath. Har MCQ ka sahi jawab hisaab ke saath diya gaya hai; short aur descriptive sawalon ke model jawab hain, aur numericals Given → formula → qeemat → jawab ki tarteeb se hal kiye gaye hain. Kitab mein MCQs ki answer key aur numericals ke jawab nahi chhape.
Multiple Choice Questions (kai jawabon mein se sahi chunein)
Q.1 Har sawal ke chaar jawab diye gaye hain. Sahi jawab chunein.

blocks.prompt:
I. Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
(Kaun sa bayan ghalat hai?)

options.text: Aik mole nitrogen gas mein Avogadro's number molecules hain
Aik mole ozone gas mein Avogadro's number molecules hain
Aik mole ozone mein Avogadro's number O atoms hain
Aik mole hydrogen gas mein Avogadro's number molecules hain

blocks.explanation: Aik mole O₃ mein 6.02 × 10²³ molecules hain; har molecule mein 3 O atoms, is liye 3 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 1.806 × 10²⁴ O atoms, Avogadro's number nahi. (a), (b), (d) durust hain.

blocks.prompt:
II. Which one of the following has maximum mass?
(Kis ka mass sab se zyada hai?)
blocks.explanation:
m = n × M
N₂: 0.5 × 28.0 = 14.0 g
NH₃: 0.5 × 17.0 = 8.5 g
He: 0.5 × 4.0 = 2.0 g
CO: 0.5 × 28.0 = 14.0 g
N₂ aur CO dono ka mass barabar aur sab se zyada (14.0 g); neeche Kitab ki ghalti dekhein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Do options barabar sahi hain: N₂ aur CO dono ka molar mass 28.0 g mol⁻¹, is liye dono ke 0.5 mol = 14.0 g. Key (a) rakhi gayi hai; (d) bhi utna hi sahi hai. In mein se aik option badalna chahiye (maslan 0.5 mol CO₂ = 22.0 g ho to sirf (d) sahi hota).

blocks.prompt:
III. Which one of the following gases will have maximum volume at STP?
(STP par kis gas ka volume sab se zyada hoga?)
blocks.explanation:
STP par volume sirf moles par munhasir hai (V = n × 22.4 dm³):
CO₂: 22/44 = 0.5 mol
N₂O: 88/44 = 2.0 mol → 44.8 dm³
CO: 28/28 = 1.0 mol
N₂: 28/28 = 1.0 mol
N₂O ke moles sab se zyada, is liye volume sab se zyada.

blocks.prompt:
IV. Which of the following contains same number of atoms as present in 12 g of carbon?
(12 g carbon mein jitne atoms hain, utne kis mein hain?)

options.text: 32 g S₈ molecules (S ka atomic mass = 32)
28 g carbon monoxide (CO ka molar mass = 28)

blocks.explanation:
12 g C = 1 mol atoms.
Fe: 28/56 = 0.5 mol atoms
Mg: 48/24 = 2 mol atoms
S₈: 32 g sulfur = 32/32 = 1 mol S atoms (1/8 mol S₈ molecules × 8)
CO: 28/28 = 1 mol molecules = 2 mol atoms
Sirf 32 g S₈ mein 1 mol (6.02 × 10²³) atoms hain.

blocks.prompt:
V. Volume at S.T.P. of 22 g of CO₂ is same as that of:
(STP par 22 g CO₂ ka volume kis ke barabar hai?)
blocks.explanation:
CO₂: 22/44 = 0.5 mol (STP par 11.2 dm³). Barabar moles ka barabar volume:
H₂: 2/2 = 1 mol
NH₃: 8.5/17 = 0.5 mol ✓
SO₂: 64/64 = 1 mol
CO: 7/28 = 0.25 mol

blocks.prompt:
VI. 4.0 g of NaOH (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) contains same number of sodium ions as are present in:
(4.0 g NaOH (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) mein jitne sodium ions hain, utne kis mein hain?)
blocks.explanation:
NaOH: 4.0/40 = 0.10 mol, yani 0.10 mol Na⁺.
Na₂CO₃: 10.6/106 = 0.10 mol → 2 × 0.10 = 0.20 mol Na⁺
NaCl: 58.5/58.5 = 1.0 mol Na⁺
Na₂SO₄: 76/142 = 0.535 mol → 1.07 mol Na⁺
NaNO₃: 85/85 = 1.0 mol Na⁺
Kisi option mein theek 0.10 mol Na⁺ nahi; (a), jis mein 0.10 mol Na₂CO₃ hai, murad jawab hai (Kitab ki ghalti dekhein).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Chhapa hua koi option bilkul durust nahi. 4.0 g NaOH mein 0.10 mol Na⁺ hain, magar 10.6 g Na₂CO₃ mein 0.20 mol Na⁺ (har formula mein do Na⁺), 58.5 g NaCl aur 85 g NaNO₃ mein 1.0 mol aur 76 g Na₂SO₄ mein 1.07 mol. Murad jawab (a) rakha gaya (0.10 mol Na₂CO₃, sab se qareeb). Utne hi Na⁺ ions 5.3 g Na₂CO₃, 5.85 g NaCl, 7.1 g Na₂SO₄ ya 8.5 g NaNO₃ mein hain. Option (c) mein "Na2SO4" subscripts ke baghair chhapa hai.

blocks.prompt:
VII. A container holds 0.5 moles of an ideal gas at STP. What is the volume of the gas in dm³?
(Aik bartan mein STP par 0.5 mole ideal gas hai. Gas ka volume dm³ mein kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: V = n × Vₘ = 0.5 mol × 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹ = 11.2 dm³

blocks.prompt:
VIII. A solution contains 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide (NaOH, molar mass = 40.0 g mol⁻¹) in 250 cm³ of solution. What is the molar concentration of this solution?
(250 cm³ solution mein 4.0 g NaOH (molar mass 40.0 g mol⁻¹) hai. Molar concentration kya hai?)

IX. A solution contains 10.0 g of an unknown solute in 250 cm³ of solution. If the molar concentration of the solution is 0.20 mol dm⁻³, what is the molar mass of the solute?
(250 cm³ solution mein 10.0 g na-maloom solute hai aur concentration 0.20 mol dm⁻³ hai. Solute ka molar mass kya hai?)
blocks.explanation:
n = C × V = 0.20 mol dm⁻³ × 0.250 dm³ = 0.050 mol
M = m/n = 10.0 g / 0.050 mol = 200 g mol⁻¹

blocks.prompt:
X. A sample of nitrogen gas (N₂, molar mass = 28.0 g mol⁻¹) has a mass of 14.0 g. How many nitrogen atoms are present in this sample?
(Nitrogen gas (N₂, molar mass 28.0 g mol⁻¹) ke 14.0 g namoone mein kitne nitrogen atoms hain?)
blocks.explanation:
n(N₂) = 14.0 / 28.0 = 0.500 mol
molecules = 0.500 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 3.01 × 10²³
atoms = 2 × 3.01 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²³ (har N₂ mein 2 atoms)

blocks.prompt:
XI. A gas has a density of 1.43 g dm⁻³ at STP. What is the molar mass of the gas? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹)
(STP par aik gas ki density 1.43 g dm⁻³ hai. Gas ka molar mass kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: M = d × Vₘ = 1.43 g dm⁻³ × 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹ = 32.0 g mol⁻¹ (gas O₂ ho sakti hai)

blocks.prompt:
XII. A gas has a density of 1.96 g dm⁻³ at STP (0 °C and 1.00 atm). What is its molecular mass? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹)
(STP (0 °C, 1.00 atm) par aik gas ki density 1.96 g dm⁻³ hai. Is ka molecular mass kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: M = d × Vₘ = 1.96 g dm⁻³ × 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹ = 43.9 g mol⁻¹ ≈ 44.0 g mol⁻¹ (maslan CO₂)

blocks.text: Q.2 Darj zail sawalon ke mukhtasar jawab dein:

blocks.prompt:
a. How is the concept of mole derived from Avogadro’s number?
Mole ka tasawwur Avogadro's number se kaise nikalta hai?
blocks.explanation: Avogadro's number (Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³) 12 g carbon-12 mein atoms ki tadaad hai. Mole woh miqdar hai jis mein itne hi zarrat (atoms, molecules, ions) hon. Yani 1 mole = 6.02 × 10²³ particles, aur us ka grams mein mass molar mass hai; n = particles/Nₐ.

blocks.prompt:
b. Define the following terms with one example in each case.
(a) Molar mass (b) Molar volume (c) Molar concentration
In istilahat ki tareef aur har aik ki misal dein: (a) Molar mass (b) Molar volume (c) Molar concentration
blocks.explanation:
(a) Molar mass: aik mole ka grams mein mass (g mol⁻¹); misal CO₂ = 44.0 g mol⁻¹.
(b) Molar volume: STP par aik mole ideal gas ka volume, 22.414 dm³ (≈ 22.4 dm³); misal 44.0 g CO₂ = 22.4 dm³.
(c) Molar concentration: aik dm³ solution mein solute ke moles (C = n/V, mol dm⁻³); misal 27.64 g K₂CO₃ (0.2 mol) 1 dm³ mein = 0.2 mol dm⁻³.

blocks.prompt:
c. What do you mean by molar volume of a gas? How Avogadro’s number is related with molar volume?
Gas ke molar volume se kya muraad hai? Avogadro's number ka molar volume se kya talluq hai?
blocks.explanation: Molar volume (Vₘ): STP (273.15 K, 1 atm) par aik mole ideal gas ka volume: 22.414 dm³. Avogadro's law ke mutabiq aik hi T aur P par barabar volumes mein barabar molecules hote hain, is liye STP par kisi bhi gas ke 22.414 dm³ mein Avogadro's number, 6.02 × 10²³, molecules hote hain.

blocks.prompt:
d. 39 g of potassium and 56 g of iron have equal number of atoms in them. Justify.
39 g potassium aur 56 g iron mein atoms barabar hain. Sabit karein.
blocks.explanation:
n(K) = 39 g / 39 g mol⁻¹ = 1 mol
n(Fe) = 56 g / 56 g mol⁻¹ = 1 mol
Har element ke aik mole mein 6.02 × 10²³ atoms, is liye dono mein atoms barabar; Fe ke atoms bhaari hain, is liye zyada mass chahiye.

blocks.prompt:
e. 4 g of He, 17 g of NH₃ and 64 g of SO₂ occupy separately the volumes of 22.414 dm³ although the sizes and masses of molecules of three gases are very different from each other.
4 g He, 17 g NH₃ aur 64 g SO₂ alag alag 22.414 dm³ ghairte hain halan ke in ke molecules ke size aur mass bohat mukhtalif hain. Wajah batayein.
blocks.explanation: Har aik aik mole hai: He 4/4, NH₃ 17/17, SO₂ 64/64 = 1 mol, yani 6.02 × 10²³ molecules. Gas mein molecules bohat door door hote hain, is liye volume molecules ki tadaad par munhasir hai, un ke size ya mass par nahi (Avogadro's law). Is liye har aik STP par 22.414 dm³ ghairti hai.

blocks.prompt:
f. Do you think that 1 mole of H₂ and 1 mole of NH₃ at 0 °C and 1 atm will have Avogadro’s number of particles?
Kya 0 °C aur 1 atm par 1 mole H₂ aur 1 mole NH₃ mein Avogadro's number particles honge?
blocks.explanation: Haan. Kisi bhi cheez ke aik mole mein har temperature aur pressure par 6.02 × 10²³ particles hote hain: 6.02 × 10²³ H₂ molecules aur 6.02 × 10²³ NH₃ molecules. 0 °C aur 1 atm (STP) par dono 22.4 dm³ bhi ghairte hain. (Atoms mukhtalif: H₂ mein 2Nₐ, NH₃ mein 4Nₐ.)

blocks.prompt:
g. What is stoichiometry? Give the basic assumptions of stoichiometric calculations.
Stoichiometry kya hai? Stoichiometric calculations ke bunyadi mafrooze (assumptions) likhein.
blocks.explanation:
Stoichiometry chemistry ki woh shakh hai jo balanced chemical equation mein reactants aur products ke miqdari (quantitative) talluq ka mutala karti hai.
Mafrooze: 1. Tamam reactants poori tarah products mein badal jaate hain. 2. Law of conservation of mass aur law of definite proportions par amal hota hai. 3. Koi side reaction nahi hota.

blocks.prompt:
h. What is a limiting reactant? How does it control the quantity of the product formed?
Limiting reactant kya hai? Yeh product ki miqdar ko kaise control karta hai?
blocks.explanation: Limiting reactant woh reactant hai jo sab se pehle khatam ho jaye aur is tarah product ki miqdar control kare. Is ke khatam hote hi reaction ruk jata hai, is liye zyada se zyada product sirf isi ki miqdar par munhasir hai; doosra reactant bach jata hai (excess). Misal 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O: 2 mol H₂ aur 2 mol O₂ mein H₂ limiting hai aur sirf 2 mol H₂O banta hai.

blocks.prompt:
i. Differentiate theoretical and actual yields. How is the percentage yield of a reaction calculated?
Theoretical aur actual yield mein farq batayein. Percentage yield kaise nikali jati hai?
blocks.explanation: % yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) × 100; % yield zyada to reaction zyada efficient.

rows: Balanced equation se hisaab kiya gaya product
Tajurbe mein asal mein hasil hone wala product
Zyada se zyada mumkin miqdar
Aam tor par theoretical se kam
Hisaab (calculation) se
Product tol kar

blocks.prompt:
j. What are the factors which are mostly responsible for the low yield of the products in chemical reactions?
Chemical reactions mein products ki kam yield ke zyada tar zimmedar factors kaun se hain?
blocks.explanation:
1. Filtration, distillation, separating funnel, dhulai, sukhane aur crystallization theek na hon to nuqsan.
2. Kuch reactants muqabil side reactions mein lag jaate hain.
3. Reaction reversible ho sakta hai; ulta (backward) reaction product kam kar deta hai.

blocks.prompt:
Q. 3 Differentiate limiting and non-limiting reactants. How a limiting reactant is determined from a balanced chemical equation and given data?
Limiting aur non-limiting reactants mein farq batayein. Balanced equation aur diye gaye data se limiting reactant kaise maloom kiya jata hai?
blocks.explanation:
Reactants aksar balanced equation ki nisbat mein nahi liye jaate; sasta reactant zyada liya jata hai taake mehnga poora badal jaye, product zyada se zyada bane aur reaction tez ho.
Limiting reactant: sab se pehle khatam; zyada se zyada product ki miqdar control karta hai; is ke khatam hone par reaction ruk jata hai.
Non-limiting (excess) reactant: reaction mukammal hone ke baad bach jata hai.
Limiting reactant maloom karna (teen qadam):
1. Diye gaye data se har reactant ke moles nikalein (n = m/M, STP par n = V/22.4 dm³, ya n = C × V).
2. Balanced equation ki mole ratio se har reactant se banne wale product ke moles nikalein.
3. Jo reactant sab se kam product de woh limiting hai; doosra excess hai.
Misal (Sample Problem 4.19): CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, 30 g CH₄ aur 50 g O₂.
n(CH₄) = 30/16 = 1.875 mol → CO₂ = 1.875 mol
n(O₂) = 50/32 = 1.563 mol → CO₂ = 1.563/2 = 0.7815 mol
O₂ kam CO₂ deta hai, is liye O₂ limiting; CO₂ = 0.7815 × 44 = 34.4 g. CH₄ istemal = 0.7815 mol, bacha = 1.875 − 0.7815 = 1.0935 mol = 17.5 g (excess).

rows: Sab se pehle (poora) khatam
Aakhir mein bach jata hai
Product ki miqdar control karta hai
Product ki miqdar control nahi karta
Hisaab mein sab se kam product deta hai
Hisaab mein zyada product deta hai
Aam tor par mehnga reactant
Aam tor par sasta, zyada miqdar mein

blocks.prompt:
Q4. Differentiate actual and theoretical yields. Why the theoretical yield is always greater than actual yield?
Actual aur theoretical yields mein farq batayein. Theoretical yield hamesha actual yield se zyada kyun hoti hai?
blocks.explanation:
Theoretical yield: limiting reactant ki di gayi miqdar se balanced equation ke zariye hisaab ki gayi zyada se zyada product ki miqdar.
Actual yield: reaction mein asal mein hasil hone wala product.
% yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) × 100; % yield zyada to reaction zyada efficient.
Theoretical yield zyada kyun:
1. Mechanical nuqsan: filtration, distillation, separating funnel, dhulai, sukhane aur crystallization theek na hon to product zaya hota hai.
2. Side reactions: kuch reactants muqabil side reactions mein doosre products bana dete hain.
3. Reversible reactions: ulta reaction product kam kar deta hai.
Hisaab mein mukammal tabdeeli aur koi side reaction na hona farz kiya jata hai jo asal reactions mein nahi hota, is liye actual yield kam hoti hai.
Misal: 3.00 g salicylic acid se aspirin ki theoretical yield 3.96 g; agar 3.15 g mile to % yield = 3.15/3.96 × 100 = 79.5 % (Sample Problem 4.20, durust ki hui).

rows: Balanced equation se hisaab
Tajurbe mein hasil
Zyada se zyada mumkin product
Theoretical se kam
Mukammal tabdeeli, koi side reaction nahi farz
Nuqsan, side aur ulte reactions se mutasir

Halaat aur maharat ke saath badalti hai

blocks.prompt:
Q.5 A solution of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is prepared by dissolving 2.00 g of solid sodium hydroxide in water to make a final volume of 250 cm³.
a) Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide used.
b) Determine the molar mass of sodium hydroxide.
c) Calculate the concentration of the sodium hydroxide solution in mol dm⁻³.
d) If more water is added to the above solution to raise the volume of solution to 500 cm³, what would be the concentration now?
2.00 g NaOH pani mein hal kar ke 250 cm³ solution banaya gaya. a) moles; b) molar mass; c) concentration mol dm⁻³ mein; d) pani dal kar 500 cm³ karne par naya concentration.
blocks.explanation:
Given: m(NaOH) = 2.00 g, V₁ = 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³, V₂ = 500 cm³ = 0.500 dm³ (Ar: Na 23.0, O 16.0, H 1.0)
b) Molar mass (pehle chahiye):
M(NaOH) = 23.0 + 16.0 + 1.0 = 40.0 g mol⁻¹
a) n = m/M
n = 2.00 g / 40.0 g mol⁻¹
n = 0.0500 mol
c) C = n/V
C = 0.0500 mol / 0.250 dm³
C = 0.200 mol dm⁻³
d) Pani milane se NaOH ke moles nahi badalte:
C₂ = n/V₂ = 0.0500 mol / 0.500 dm³
C₂ = 0.100 mol dm⁻³ (volume do guna to concentration aadha; C₁V₁ = C₂V₂)

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Hamesha cm³ ko dm³ mein badlein: 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³, is liye 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³. Part (a) ke liye molar mass (b) pehle nikalna parta hai.

blocks.prompt:
Q.6 Ammonia gas (NH₃) reacts with oxygen gas (O₂) according to the following balanced equation:
4NH₃(g) + 5O₂(g) ⟶ 4NO(g) + 6H₂O(g)
In an experiment, 34.0 g of ammonia is reacted with 80.0 g of oxygen.
a) Determine the limiting reactant.
b) Calculate the maximum mass of nitrogen monoxide (NO) that can be formed.
c) Calculate the mass of the excess reactant remaining after the reaction is complete. (Relative atomic masses: H = 1.0, N = 14.0, O = 16.0)
34.0 g NH₃ aur 80.0 g O₂ ka reaction: a) limiting reactant; b) NO ka zyada se zyada mass; c) bache hue excess reactant ka mass.
blocks.explanation:
Given: m(NH₃) = 34.0 g, m(O₂) = 80.0 g; M(NH₃) = 14.0 + 3(1.0) = 17.0 g mol⁻¹, M(O₂) = 32.0 g mol⁻¹, M(NO) = 14.0 + 16.0 = 30.0 g mol⁻¹
Moles:
n(NH₃) = 34.0 / 17.0 = 2.00 mol
n(O₂) = 80.0 / 32.0 = 2.50 mol
a) Har reactant se NO:
NH₃ se: 4 mol NH₃ → 4 mol NO, is liye 2.00 mol NH₃ → 2.00 mol NO
O₂ se: 5 mol O₂ → 4 mol NO, is liye 2.50 mol O₂ → (4/5) × 2.50 = 2.00 mol NO
Dono barabar, 2.00 mol NO dete hain: reactants theek 4 : 5 (2.00 : 2.50) ki nisbat mein hain. Koi excess nahi; dono poore khatam (koi aik limiting reactant nahi).
b) m(NO) = n × M = 2.00 mol × 30.0 g mol⁻¹ = 60.0 g
c) 2.00 mol NH₃ ke liye O₂ = (5/4) × 2.00 = 2.50 mol = saari li gayi O₂.
Bacha hua excess reactant = 0 g.
Jaanch: 34.0 + 80.0 = 114.0 g = 60.0 g NO + 54.0 g H₂O (3.00 mol × 18.0).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Data ke mutabiq reactants bilkul equation ki nisbat mein hain: 34.0 g NH₃ (2.00 mol) aur 80.0 g O₂ (2.50 mol) = 4 : 5. Is liye koi limiting ya excess reactant nahi, aur hissa (c) ka jawab 0 g hai. Agar maslan 100 g O₂ (3.13 mol) hoti to NH₃ limiting hota, NO phir bhi 60.0 g banta aur 20.0 g O₂ bachti.

blocks.prompt:
Q.7 When iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃) reacts with carbon monoxide (CO) in a blast furnace, iron metal (Fe) is produced according to the following equation:
Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) ⟶ 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g)
If 1.00 kg of iron(III) oxide is reacted with excess carbon monoxide, and 650 g of iron is obtained, what is the percentage yield of iron? (Aᵣ of O = 16.0, Fe = 55.8)
1.00 kg Fe₂O₃ zyada CO se reaction kare aur 650 g iron mile to iron ki percentage yield kya hai?
blocks.explanation:
Given: m(Fe₂O₃) = 1.00 kg = 1000 g, Fe ki actual yield = 650 g; Aᵣ: Fe = 55.8, O = 16.0
M(Fe₂O₃) = 2(55.8) + 3(16.0) = 111.6 + 48.0 = 159.6 g mol⁻¹
n(Fe₂O₃) = 1000 g / 159.6 g mol⁻¹ = 6.266 mol
Equation se 1 mol Fe₂O₃ → 2 mol Fe:
n(Fe) = 2 × 6.266 = 12.53 mol
Fe ki theoretical yield = 12.53 mol × 55.8 g mol⁻¹ = 699 g
% yield = (actual / theoretical) × 100
% yield = (650 g / 699 g) × 100
% yield = 93.0 %

blocks.prompt:
Q.8 PbSO₄ is precipitated when aqueous solutions of Na₂SO₄ and Pb(NO₃)₂ are mixed. Calculate the mass of PbSO₄ formed when 1.25 dm³ of 0.05 M Pb(NO₃)₂ and 2 dm³ of 0.025 M Na₂SO₄ are mixed.
1.25 dm³ 0.05 M Pb(NO₃)₂ aur 2 dm³ 0.025 M Na₂SO₄ milane par kitna PbSO₄ banega?
blocks.explanation:
Given: Pb(NO₃)₂: C = 0.05 mol dm⁻³, V = 1.25 dm³; Na₂SO₄: C = 0.025 mol dm⁻³, V = 2 dm³; M(PbSO₄) = 303.3 g mol⁻¹
Na₂SO₄(aq) + Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2NaNO₃(aq)
Net ionic: Pb²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s) (1 : 1)
n = C × V
n(Pb²⁺) = 0.05 × 1.25 = 0.0625 mol
n(SO₄²⁻) = 0.025 × 2 = 0.050 mol
SO₄²⁻ (0.050 mol) Pb²⁺ (0.0625 mol) se kam hai, is liye SO₄²⁻ (Na₂SO₄) limiting reactant hai.
n(PbSO₄) = 0.050 mol
m(PbSO₄) = 0.050 mol × 303.3 g mol⁻¹ = 15.2 g
(Bacha Pb²⁺: 0.0625 − 0.050 = 0.0125 mol.) Yeh kitab ka Sample Problem 4.18 hai; us ka jawab 15.2 g is se milta hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: M (molarity) = mol dm⁻³. Do solutions milane wale sawal mein pehle har ion ke moles (C × V) nikalein, phir 1 : 1 ratio mein kam moles wala limiting hai.
